sources.claim_locator: Status; Superseding; Board Approval; History > Published; opening abstract
sources.source_type: Official standard catalog status and abstract
sources.source_claims_supported: The official IEEE catalog lists ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207-2026 as an active standard, states that it supersedes 12207-2017, and lists board approval on 2026-02-12 and publication on 2026-04-15. The catalog abstract describes a common software life-cycle process framework and says users may compose a suitable life-cycle model from selected processes/stages.
sources.source_limitations: Catalog status and abstract only; the full normative clauses were not inspected. This does not establish which clauses an organization adopted, whether the standard is contractually or legally binding for a project, or whether any implementation conforms.

sources.claim_locator: “Choose your starting point”; “Compare agent runtime options”; sections describing Agents API and Agents SDK.
sources.source_claims_supported: The page describes agents as systems that can plan and complete tasks using tools, work with other agents, and maintain context; it compares runtime options by orchestration, state management, tools, and execution environment.
sources.source_limitations: Product documentation describes OpenAI runtime options and capabilities, not a vendor-neutral agent definition or a tested implementation. It does not establish that every agent must use tools, multi-agent collaboration, or persistent state.

sources.claim_locator: “Core benefits” section, including bullets on mixing deterministic and agentic steps, persistence, human-in-the-loop, and memory.
sources.source_claims_supported: The documentation states LangGraph provides infrastructure for long-running, stateful workflows or agents and supports mixing deterministic and agentic steps, persistence/resumption, human oversight, and short- and long-term memory.
sources.source_limitations: Describes the LangGraph framework's stated capabilities; it is not a general requirement or independently tested evidence of those capabilities in a particular application.

sources.claim_locator: “Tracing,” “Traces and spans,” and “Default tracing” sections in docs/tracing.md at the stated commit.
sources.source_claims_supported: The SDK documentation says tracing records events during agent runs, including model generations, tool calls, handoffs, guardrails, and custom events; it defines traces as workflow-level operations composed of spans and lists the operations traced by default.
sources.source_limitations: This is implementation-specific SDK documentation, not general agent architecture guidance. Tracing is enabled by default in the described SDK, but may be disabled; the documentation notes that tracing is unavailable for organizations using APIs under a Zero Data Retention policy. Repository file and current main HEAD were inspected; no software was executed.

sources.claim_locator: Page introduction and “Agentic AI – Threats and Mitigations” heading; dated February 17, 2025.
sources.source_claims_supported: The page describes the resource as the first in a series of OWASP Agentic Security Initiative guides, intended to provide a threat-model-based reference to emerging agentic threats and discuss mitigations.
sources.source_limitations: The page's stated purpose does not by itself verify any particular threat scenario or mitigation's effectiveness. It is guidance, not a formal standard or evidence from a tested system.
